content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The entry's core identification — that the 'lost sheep' denotes the scattered house of Israel whom the Messiah is sent to seek and regather — is carried directly by the sole printed proof text, Matthew 15:24 ('I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel'), which is an explicit in-text definition of the phrase. The elaborations printed in the entry are each independently attested in the supplied evidence: 'scattered' and 'mingled with the nations' by Hosea 7:8 ('Ephraim... hath mixed himself among the people') and the exile texts the common interpretation itself cites (Jeremiah 50:6; Ezekiel 34); 'sought and regathered' by Ezekiel 34:11-16 and Ezekiel 37:21-22 and by the sending language of Matthew 15:24 itself; and the generalization 'more generally, any unrepentant sinner' by Luke 15:3-7 / Matthew 18:12-14, which is exactly the mainstream consensus reading. The strongest counter — that the primary referent is the straying sinner generally, with Israel a secondary contextual scope — does not contradict the entry, because the entry explicitly includes the sinner-general sense; the dispute is one of ordering emphasis, not of rival referents. No supplied text is inexplicable on the entry's core, whereas the entry uniquely explains why Matthew's Jesus twice restricts the phrase to 'the house of Israel.' FULL support with PERSUADED verdict.","book_core_identification":"The 'lost sheep' are the scattered house of Israel — lost among the nations and sought/regathered by God through the Messiah (Matt 15:24) — with a general extension to any straying, unrepentant sinner.","book_secondary_elaborations":["Israel was 'mingled with the nations' (scattered/mixed among the peoples, per Hosea 7:8; Jer 50:6; Ezek 34)","The lost sheep are 'sought and regathered' (divine initiative to seek and restore, per Ezek 34:11-16; Ezek 37:21-22; Matt 15:24)","'More generally, any unrepentant sinner' (the Luke 15:3-7 / Matt 18:12-14 sense recognized as the mainstream primary meaning)"],"unsupported_glossary_assertions":[],"chapter_only_objections":["The chapter's identification of Ephraim's melo ha-goyim (Gen 48:19) with Paul's 'fulness of the Gentiles' (Rom 11:25), implying the Gentile church is scattered Ephraim regathered, is a chapter-level typological argument not asserted in the glossary entry.","The chapter's reading of Zechariah's two olive trees and Revelation's two witnesses as two covenant peoples (Judah and Joseph-Ephraim) is a chapter-only claim.","The chapter's claim that Jacob/Israel naming encodes the crooked-heart-made-straight pattern in every believer, and that Israel 'was never a bloodline,' is broader than and separate from the glossary entry."],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The mainstream reading in Responses A-D: the lost sheep is primarily the individual sinner (or humanity generally) who strays from God and is sought and joyfully restored by the divine Shepherd (Luke 15:3-7; Matt 18:12-14; Isa 53:6; Ps 119:176; Ezek 34:11-16; 1 Pet 2:25), with 'the lost sheep of the house of Israel' (Matt 10:6; 15:24) treated as a narrower, context-specific application defining the initial scope of Jesus' mission.","counter_core_identification":"The lost sheep = any straying sinner sought and restored by God/Christ; the Israel reference in Matthew 10:6 and 15:24 is a subset application of the same image.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"SAME_CORE_BROADER","material_core_denial":"No material denial exists. The counter does not assert that the lost sheep cannot refer to scattered Israel; every supplied common-interpretation response lists the Israel referent as a 'common' alternative grounded in the very verse the entry prints (Matt 15:24). The counter and the entry differ only in which sense is foregrounded, and the entry itself incorporates the counter's sense in its 'more generally' clause. Both identifications can be true of the same image, so no contradiction of the core arises.","counter_case":["Luke 15:3-7 explicitly interprets the lost sheep as 'one sinner that repenteth,' making the sinner-general sense the dominant NT parabolic usage.","Isaiah 53:6, Psalm 119:176, and 1 Peter 2:25 extend the straying-sheep image to humanity and believers generally, not ethnic Israel alone.","Matthew 10:6 and 15:24 can be read as a temporary mission-scope statement rather than a definition of the symbol's primary referent.","The overwhelming ecumenical consensus reads the image as individual sinner sought by God, with the Israel sense secondary."],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Matthew 15:24, the entry's printed proof text, is an explicit in-text definition: 'the lost sheep of the house of Israel' — the entry simply reads the verse's own words, requiring zero interpretive steps for its core.","The entry explains the specifically national OT background the counter also cites (Jer 50:6 'my people have been lost sheep'; Ezek 34's scattered flock of Israel), where 'lost sheep' first denotes the covenant nation among the nations.","'Mingled with the nations' is directly attested by Hosea 7:8 ('Ephraim... hath mixed himself among the people'), giving the entry's phrasing a concrete textual anchor.","'Sought and regathered' matches Ezekiel 34:11-16 and 37:21-22 verbatim in substance: God searches for scattered Israel and gathers them into one.","The entry does not exclude the mainstream reading; it prints it ('more generally, any unrepentant sinner'), so it accounts for Luke 15 and Matthew 18 as well as the counter does, while also explaining the Israel-restricted texts the counter must demote."],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["The counter better matches the frequency of popular usage, where Luke 15's sinner-general sense dominates preaching and devotion.","The counter avoids any risk of sliding toward lost-tribes/British-Israelist identifications (though the printed entry itself makes no such modern-nation claim)."],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Matthew 15:24 (KJV excerpt) — explicit identification of the lost sheep as 'the house of Israel'","Jeremiah 50:6 and Ezekiel 34:11-16 (cited in both common-interpretation responses) — 'lost sheep' as scattered national Israel whom God seeks and regathers","Hosea 7:8 (chapter evidence) — Ephraim 'mixed himself among the people,' supporting 'mingled with the nations'","Luke 15:3-7 / Matthew 18:12-14 — supporting the entry's general extension to the straying sinner"],"unresolved_objections":["The entry foregrounds the Israel sense and demotes the sinner-general sense to 'more generally,' inverting the emphasis of majority usage; this is an ordering preference, not an unsupported assertion, since both senses are printed and both are textually attested.","The phrase 'unrepentant sinner' is slightly stronger than Luke 15's 'sinner that repenteth,' but it accurately describes the sheep's state while lost, before restoration, so it is not a material error."],"confidence":"high"}
